note: Scores written by Claude (not by the app's model route) from the application text only, using the rubric anchors in Settings and the fund's own rules (founder owns the hardest risk; groundwork before product; a missing number lowers the score; evidence over pedigree). No web research was run, so nothing is verified outside the application and no confidence is 'high'. Review these; they are a first pass, not a decision.

claims.margin: Gross margin 48% after COGS and packaging. Blended CAC INR 340
claims.channel_cac: Paid social 45% of new customers (CAC INR 410), quick commerce 25% (INR 290 after promos)
claims.copacker: All made by one co-packer in Hosur
claims.founders: 6 years in category and brand roles at a large packaged-food company
claims.moat: Cohort data tracked Yes n/a Unknown

C1.why: Six years of brand and category work plus five in supply chain suits a consumer-brand pair, but nothing is verified outside the application.

C2.why: They name the single co-packer and rising paid-social cost as their own risks, but have no second source yet.

C3.why: Repeat rises each month (31%, 34%, 38%) on a cohort of 3,100 customers.

C4.why: They volunteer cohort repeat, margin and CAC by channel without being asked, but the market size is ten times what their own inputs give.

C5.why: A INR 2.5 Cr raise mostly for inventory and working capital fits a pre-seed cheque.

C6.why: Taste-first and millet-based is a position, but the deck gives no answer to a well-funded copier.
C6.gap: No answer to a funded copier

claims.rev: INR 9.8 L across the three clinics in October 2026
claims.breakeven: The first clinic reached monthly breakeven in month 8
claims.capex: INR 28 L per clinic, funded by angels and a INR 40 L bank loan
claims.use: Five new clinics, working capital, team and systems
claims.ops: 6 years in operations at a hospital chain
claims.survey: Spend per household is our estimate from clinic billing and a 90-household survey
claims.risks: Capital intensity, doctor retention, and slower ramp in new locations

C1.why: A family doctor and a hospital-operations lead cover the clinical and site sides, with no field work shown beyond the clinics themselves.

C2.why: They name capital intensity and doctor retention as their own risks and fund capex with angels and a bank loan.

C3.why: Revenue grew each month to INR 9.8 L and the first clinic reached breakeven in month 8.

C4.why: Their figures agree between form and deck, the market arithmetic is right, and they say which numbers are estimates.

C5.why: Five more clinics at INR 28 L each is a capital-heavy model that does not fit a pre-seed cheque, and healthcare is outside the areas the fund backs.

C6.why: Neighbourhood clinics are easy to copy and the file gives no answer to a funded chain.

claims.cred_deck: Ex-Goldman Sachs. Ex-Google. MBA, IIM Ahmedabad
claims.cred_form: Summer analyst internship (10 weeks) at an investment bank
claims.vendor: 5-month contract role through a vendor at a large technology company
claims.tier2: MBA at a tier-2 business school (2022 to 2024)

claims.funding: Advances are funded by our partner NBFC's balance sheet under an agreement in principle
claims.cofounder: A co-founder left in July 2026 and has moved on
claims.tam: TAM INR 14,400 Cr 10M gig and shift workers

C1.why: The deck says Ex-Goldman, Ex-Google and IIM while the form describes a 10-week internship, a 5-month vendor contract and a tier-2 school; there is no field work shown.

C2.why: Advances rest on a partner NBFC's balance sheet under an agreement in principle, with no loss figure and a named regulatory risk.

C3.why: INR 38 L has been advanced, but the form shows one live client and two pilots while the deck says three live.

C4.why: Team size (5 against 12), live clients (1 against 3) and the market size (ten times too small for its inputs) all disagree.

C5.why: A lending book needs capital the cheque cannot give, and a co-founder has left.

C6.why: The why-now (UPI, gig work) is reasonable but the business is exposed to rules on digital lending.

claims.pilots: 11 pilots started since March 2026. 6 converted to paid, across 140 sensors (average 23 per customer)
claims.cac: Cost per paid customer is about INR 73,000 (11 pilots at INR 4.4 L / 6)
claims.value: These figures are customer-reported, not audited
claims.tam: TAM INR 16,200 Cr ~300K manufacturing MSMEs with 20+ motors x 60 sensors x INR 9,000 a year
claims.avg: Average customer: 23 sensors and INR 3.1 L first-year gross profit
claims.visits: From visits to 38 plants in the Pune and Coimbatore clusters
claims.founders: IIT Madras, mechanical engineering. 5 years as a reliability engineer at an engine maker
claims.hardware: Hardware INR 9,500 per sensor. Cost to us: INR 3,200
claims.channels: 3 of 6 paid customers came through a cluster association, 2 through a pump distributor, 1 direct
claims.risks: Sensor accuracy across motor types, hardware supply, and longer sales cycles in larger plants

C1.why: A reliability engineer who visited 38 plants before building, with an embedded-systems co-founder who designed the board.

C2.why: They name sensor accuracy and supply as theirs and say plainly that the value figures are customer-reported, not audited.

C3.why: Six of 11 pilots converted to paid across 140 sensors, through three different channels.

C4.why: CAC is worked out openly from pilot cost, but the market size assumes 60 sensors a customer when their own average is 23.

C5.why: Hardware sells at about three times its cost and a INR 2.2 Cr raise fits a pre-seed hardware company.

C6.why: Cheap sensors and a model that learns each motor in 14 days undercut INR 40,000 imported monitors, with live pilots to show it.

claims.users: 1,900 registered. 1,100 have paid at least once
claims.volume: INR 6.1 Cr paid since July 2026 across 2,400 payments
claims.net: After the 0.9% we pay the payment partner, net revenue is INR 5.5 L
claims.single: We rely on a single payment aggregator partner
claims.rules: Banks and card networks have changed rules on rent payments before, and a change would hit us directly
claims.cac: We have not measured cost per paying user
claims.founders: Product manager at a fintech for 4 years; launched two payments features

C1.why: A fintech product manager and a growth lead are relevant, with no groundwork with landlords or renters shown.

C2.why: The hardest risk, a partner or card network changing the rules, sits entirely outside their control and they say it would hit them directly.

C3.why: 1,100 of 1,900 users have paid at least once and 2,400 payments came from them, so some repeat exists, but it is not broken out.

C4.why: The deck shows INR 11 L as revenue while the form says net is INR 5.5 L, and cost per paying user is not measured.
C4.gap: Cost per paying user not measured

C5.why: The raise is small enough, but a 0.9% net margin on volume leaves little to build a company on.

C6.why: 'No direct competitors' is an overclaim and nothing protects them from a bank or aggregator doing this itself.
C6.gap: No answer to a copier or the partner

claims.volume: INR 86 Cr payment volume in October 2026. Net revenue INR 78 L
claims.unit: CAC INR 14,500 per SME, payback 7 months, gross margin 58%, net revenue retention 112%
claims.founders: 10 years in transaction banking; led SME product at a private bank
claims.risk: Credit losses on financed invoices, dependence on NBFC partners, regulation of digital lending
claims.financing: invoice financing funded by NBFC partners
claims.tam: TAM INR 9.4 lakh Cr 2.1M B2B-trading SMEs x INR 4.5 Cr annual B2B payments
claims.avgpay: Average SME pays INR 6,800 a month in fees and financing charges

C1.why: Ten years in transaction banking and eight in payments engineering fit this business well.

C2.why: Financing is funded by NBFC partners and credit losses are named as a risk, but no loss rate is given.
C2.gap: No loss rate for a business that finances invoices

C3.why: 1,150 SMEs, INR 86 Cr of monthly volume and 112% net revenue retention.

C4.why: Payback is stated as 7 months but their own CAC, fees and margin give about 3.7, and the market size is ten times too small for its inputs.

C5.why: A Series A raise of INR 30 Cr is far beyond a pre-seed cheque. This is outside the fund's range, not a weak application.

C6.why: Payments plus financing for SMEs is a clear need, but the file does not say what protects it from larger players.

claims.retailers_form: 42 retailers onboarded, 22 of whom have ordered more than once
claims.cac_form: Our CAC is under INR 2,000 per store
claims.cac_calc: CAC = INR 40,000 field cost / 14 stores onboarded in October
claims.credit_form: Credit is provided through our NBFC partner. We take the first-loss risk
claims.credit_deck: Pilot with 12 retailers, funded from our own capital for now
claims.defaults: Defaults to date: None so far
claims.assume: INR 1.2 L monthly purchases per store from our 60 owner interviews
claims.founders: 8 years in FMCG distribution and field operations
claims.interviews: Based on 60 owner interviews in Karimnagar and Warangal, June to July 2026

C1.why: Eight years in FMCG distribution and 60 owner interviews before building is the groundwork the fund looks for.

C2.why: They say they take first loss, but the form says credit comes through an NBFC partner while the deck says it is their own capital with the NBFC still in discussion.
C2.gap: Who funds the credit book is unclear

C3.why: 22 of 38 retailers have reordered, but it is one town and INR 3.8 L of monthly volume.

C4.why: Retailers (42 against 38) and CAC (under 2,000 against 2,860) differ, and the market assumes INR 1.2 L a month per store against about INR 10,000 actual.

C5.why: A INR 2 Cr raise fits, but 40% goes to a credit book the company may not be able to fund.

C6.why: A vernacular, small-town focus is a real edge over metro marketplaces, but the file does not address a better-funded copier.

claims.cac: CAC about INR 48,000 per team, including founder time at a nominal salary
claims.crm: 6 years as a product lead at a CRM software company
claims.speech: 4 years in speech ML at a speech-technology company
claims.comp: Gong and similar global tools, and meeting note-takers like Otter and Fireflies
claims.acq: Founder-led outbound brought 9 teams, referrals 5 and CRM consultants 2

C1.why: A CRM product lead and a speech-ML engineer fit the product, with sales groundwork shown only through founder-led outbound.

C2.why: They name recording rules, accuracy and customer concentration as their own risks.

C3.why: 16 paying teams in four months, 9 of them from founder-led outbound.

C4.why: CAC counts founder time honestly, but MRR differs between form (1.9 L) and deck (2.1 L) and 340 seats at INR 500 is 1.7 L, matching neither.

C5.why: 70% gross margin and a five-month payback suit a INR 2 Cr software raise.

C6.why: Code-mixed Indian languages are a real edge over global tools, but a funded rival could add them.

claims.revenue: Total booking value INR 38.6 L. We earn a 12% commission, so revenue is INR 4.6 L
claims.repeat: 14% of families have booked a second trip
claims.cac: Paid acquisition is about INR 640 per booking
claims.manual: Bookings are confirmed manually on WhatsApp
claims.deck_vague: served thousands of travellers across Rajasthan and Uttarakhand, with 3x growth

claims.templates: The itinerary uses a language model and 40 hand-built route templates
claims.deck_raise: We are raising funds to grow
claims.risks: Quality of local partners, seasonality and manual operations that do not yet scale

C1.why: Ten years running a family travel agency for over 3,000 families is real customer groundwork, though unverified.

C2.why: The form names partner quality and manual operations as risks, but the deck does not mention that bookings are confirmed by hand.

C3.why: 410 bookings and a 14% second-trip rate on a small base.

C4.why: The deck says 'thousands of travellers' and '3x growth' with no figures, while the form says about 1,300 travellers; the form's own numbers are specific and consistent.

C5.why: A small raise fits, but revenue of INR 4.6 L on INR 38.6 L of bookings is thin, and the deck states no raise amount.

C6.why: Forty hand-built templates plus a language model is easy to copy and the file does not say what protects it.
